input.question: Which organisms have little to no role in the ecosystem?
input.ground_truth: To a certain degree, all organisms have a role in the ecosystem. Whether it's being food for a single species, or keeping predators in check, if the species is able to continue to exist in nature, it has an important role - so I'd say the ones with little to no role are the ones that are extinct (not including the ones that have been killed off, or have gone extinct due to environmental disasters). Kind of related: I've heard arguments that pandas are relatively useless in their environment? Cause they're not the sole staple diet of any one species, nor do they control prey-population sizes, but I'm open to hearing other input!

Okay, let’s imagine the ecosystem is like a big playground. On the playground, there are lots of kids (these are the different animals, plants, and tiny creatures). Most kids have a job to help the playground work well—like picking up trash, planting flowers, or playing games that help everyone have fun.

But sometimes, there are a few toys or things on the playground that don’t really do anything. Maybe a broken toy that no one plays with, or a tiny pebble that just sits there and doesn’t help or hurt anyone.

In the ecosystem, some organisms are like those toys. They don’t really help and they don’t really hurt the playground (the ecosystem). They just live there and don’t do much for the other living things or for the environment. Sometimes these organisms are called “functionally redundant” or “not very important” to the ecosystem.

But even these little organisms are still part of the playground—they just don’t have a big job to do.
